title: basicly change-shape handoff artifact
description: What CLASSIFY hands DECOMPOSE (factory loop requirements 8, 8.2). One artifact per decompose event - not per requirement - so a leaf has one and an epic has one at each level of its tree. Every field is derived from an AST, never authored: it exists because the decomposer can otherwise see only scope globs, and slicing by file adjacency is horizontal slicing, which produces children with no consumer-visible behaviour to demonstrate. A derivation cannot fail a judgement, so it either parses or reports that it could not.

schema_version.description: Artifact-format version; bump only when a consumer's contract changes.

issue.description: The unit about to be decomposed. One change-shape per decompose event, so the id is what distinguishes an epic's shape from its child's.

call_tree.description: What calls what, one edge per entry. This is the structure that lets the decomposer cut end to end instead of by directory. Empty is a declared answer - a change reaching no call site - and the key being absent is silence, which is why it is required.

caller.description: The qualified name on the calling side. Named rather than pointed at by path, because the cut this informs follows behaviour and not files.

callee.description: The qualified name on the called side, so an edge read on its own still says which direction the dependency runs.

file_tree.description: The file-tree diff the requirement names: what appears and what moves. Both halves are required because a move read as an appearance plus a disappearance invents a new file the plan would then slice around.

appears.description: Paths this change introduces. Empty is a declared answer for a change that only edits what exists; absence would be indistinguishable from a derivation that never ran.

moves.description: Paths this change relocates, each with both ends. Empty is a declared answer, for the same reason appears carries one.

from.description: Where the file was, so a scope glob written against the old tree can be recognised as stale rather than as unmatched.

to.description: Where the file lands, so the plan's scope globs are declared against the tree BUILD will actually see.

new_public_functions.description: The signatures this change adds to the public surface. Required because a new public signature is the thing the integrity downgrade reads and the thing a consumer eventually calls; empty is a declared answer for a change that adds none.

path.description: The file the definition lands in, so the signature can be checked against the tree rather than taken on trust.

name.description: The qualified name, which is how the call tree above refers to it; without it the two halves of this artifact cannot be joined.

signature.description: The declaration as the AST reports it. The signature and not a summary of it, because this artifact's value is that no model composed it.
